newsitem.title: USA: Liz Claiborne income rises more than expected.
newsitem.headline: Liz Claiborne income rises more than expected.

text.p: Liz Claiborne Inc. said Monday its profits jumped more than expected in the first quarter on strong sales of its casual wear, mens sportswear and Dana Buchman line of upscale women's clothing.

Net income rose to $42.1 million, or 59 cents a share, in the quarter ended April 5 from $35.9 million, or 49 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Earnings per share surpassed analysts' consensus estimates of 56 cents.
Sales rose to a record $596.6 million from $556.6 million, partly because the 1997 period had 14 weeks while the year-ago period had 13 weeks, the company said.
"Our momentum built steadily throughout 1996 and has extended into 1997, with positive overall performance at retail," said Paul Charron, chairman and chief executive.

"We are encouraged by our progress in product development and are continuing to successfully drive our cost reduction efforts, the reengineering of key business processes and the technology initiatives which are key to furthering the transformation of Liz Claiborne."
Liz Claiborne, based in New York, designs and manufactures women's fashion apparel and accessories, men's apparel and furnishings, and makes fragrances for women and men.
Its stock was unchanged at $46 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
